protocol.py: 5 biology problems (4 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was set only after its liquids were
used
   line 55:  p300.aspirate(132, buffer_loc)
   At line 55 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1, on a
   temperature module that the protocol sets to 4 C only at line 89, after buffer (carrier),
   fwd primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 13 more had already
   been used: the robot pipetted there 20 times before the call. A temperature module stays
   at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so every one of those transfers
   happened on a warm block. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [307ed34590ae]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 62:  p20.dispense(6.6, master_mix_loc)
   At line 62 the robot put polymerase into well A6 in slot 1. Take well A6 in slot 1: at
   that moment it held only 132 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at
   line 80, to make the 270.6 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is
   shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the
   water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat
   buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then
   cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: well A6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to well A6 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix
   it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [72e9515ab789]

3. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: A pipette too small to mix well A6 in slot 1: 20 ul at most in
303.6 ul
   line 85:  p20.mix(5, 20, master_mix_loc)
   At line 85 the tip mixes well A6 in slot 1 with 5 strokes of 20 ul in a well holding
   303.6 ul. The P20 can draw at most 20 ul, under a fifth of the well: no stroke it can
   make will mix this well, however many times. Integra draws over 80% of the well five
   times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well A6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix with a bigger pipette (a P300 for this well): at least 5 strokes of 242.9 ul,
   `mix(5, 242.9, well)`.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [6920074c5304]

4. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Too few strokes to mix 12 wells: 2 × 20 ul in 25 ul
   line 104:  p20.mix(2, 20, plate[f"A{i+1}"])
   At line 104 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 4 with
   2 strokes of 20 ul in a well holding 25 ul (this line did it 12 times). The well holds
   more than the p20_single_gen2 can draw, so the stroke is judged against the pipette's 20
   ul. Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five
   times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix with the pipette's full volume (20 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 20, well)`, or
   use a bigger pipette.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [0432b6c28ca6]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 12 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 95:  p300.dispense(23, well)
   At line 95 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 4), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 4 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [8c4f3cd0af54]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
